message.reasoning_content:
<plan>
CHANGES:

Change #1: Model Architecture — Wide & Deep + Multi-Seed Bagging over FT-Transformer with DART-style deep ensemble
- What: Replace the single FT-Transformer with an ensemble of 5 FT-Transformers (varying seeds, d_token, n_layers) AND augment with a strong gradient-boosted tree (LightGBM if available, else sklearn HistGradientBoosting) trained on the same engineered one-hot/ordinal features. Predict by averaging probabilities (rank-averaged). Trees capture axis-aligned interactions that transformers under-use; transformers capture higher-order smooth interactions.
- Why: Tabular coupon data is dominated by categorical interactions (coupon × time × income × direction) that tree models handle natively and near-optimally at this scale (8k rows). A pure 1-layer FT-Transformer with only 5 folds is highly variance-bound at n=8117; blending a strong GBDT removes that variance and usually lifts accuracy 1-3 points on this style of dataset.

Change #2: Feature Engineering — add ordinal & cross features trees love
- What: Add explicit `coupon_x_direction`, `time_x_expiration`, `income_x_coupon`, `age_bucket_x_has_children`, plus target-free aggregate stats (per-coupon count/mean-ordinal) fit only on train. Add OHE for trees.
- Why: The tree half of the ensemble needs split-friendly interactions; the transformer also benefits because these interactions become single-token categorical fields.

KEEP UNCHANGED:
- Random seed 42
- Stratified fold structure
- CLI/subcommand contract, output format, threshold search on OOF only, label encoding.
</plan>"
